title: Main Argument and Supporting Points
summary: إزاي تطلّع الفكرة الأساسية اللي الكاتب عايز يقنعك بيها، والأسباب والأدلة اللي بيسندها بيها.

blocks.text: الدرس ده عن إيه؟

text: In an argument text (an opinion article, an essay, a discursive text), the **main argument** is the writer's central opinion. The **supporting points** are the reasons and the evidence the writer gives to make us believe it.

blocks.text: أي مقال رأي (opinion article) أو نص فيه نقاش، الكاتب بيبقى عايز يقنعك بحاجة واحدة كبيرة. الحاجة دي اسمها **main argument** يعني «الرأي الأساسي». وعلشان يقنعك بيها بيجيب **أسباب** و**أدلة**، ودي اسمها **supporting points** يعني «النقط اللي بتسند الرأي».

في الكتاب المهارة دي موجودة في **Unit 1: Living Well in a Complex World** (مقال رأي عن السوشيال ميديا وصورتنا عن نفسنا، ومقال عن المسؤولية الشخصية والصحة)، وفي **Unit 4** (مقال عن الأبلكيشنز والتركيز، ومقال عن خدع الأوكازيون). وفي جدول التقييم الذاتي آخر Unit 1 الكتاب بيقول بالنص: «identify the main argument and supporting points in an opinion article». وفي أسئلة الفهم بيسأل: **What is the writer's main argument about…?**
والمهارة دي مربوطة جدًا بطريقة الكتاب **JRE** (Justify – Reasoning – Evidence): الكاتب نفسه بيعمل JRE وهو بيكتب، وإنت بتفكّك الـ JRE بتاعه وإنت بتقرا.
الفرق بين Topic و Main Argument و Supporting Points

text: The **topic** is what the text is about (one or two words). The **main argument** is what the writer thinks about the topic (a full sentence with an opinion). The **supporting points** explain why.

blocks.text: ده أهم حتة في الدرس، وأغلب الطلبة بيتلخبطوا فيها. خد المثال ده:

rows: رأي الكاتب في الموضوع، جملة كاملة
Schools should teach students how to use social media wisely instead of banning it.
Bans do not work because teenagers find other ways online.
دليل: رقم، دراسة، مثال، كلام خبير
A survey found that 70% of students used social media at school despite a ban.
This shows that rules alone cannot change habits.

blocks.text: يعني بالعربي: **الموضوع** = «السوشيال ميديا». **الرأي** = «المدارس لازم تعلّم الطلبة يستخدموها صح بدل ما تمنعها». الموضوع مفيهوش رأي، لكن الـ main argument لازم يكون فيه **رأي** ممكن حد يختلف معاه.

blocks.title: حيلة: اختبار «أنا موافق / مش موافق»
items: لو قريت الجملة وتقدر تقول عليها «**أنا موافق**» أو «**أنا مش موافق**» يبقى دي ممكن تكون main argument.
لو الجملة مجرد معلومة (زي «Teenagers need 8-10 hours of sleep») يبقى دي **evidence** أو detail، مش رأي.
لو هي كلمة أو اتنين من غير فعل (زي «sleep and health») يبقى دي **topic** بس.

blocks.text: شكل مقال الرأي من جوه: «الشجرة»

text: Most argument texts follow the same plan: introduction with the main argument → body paragraphs, each with one supporting point and evidence → a counter-argument and a reply → a conclusion that restates the main argument.

blocks.text: تخيل المقال **شجرة**: الجذع هو الـ main argument، والفروع هي الـ supporting points، والورق اللي على كل فرع هو الأدلة والأمثلة. ولما بتقرا، إنت بتحاول ترسم الشجرة دي في دماغك.

rows: الكاتب بيشد انتباهك، وغالبًا آخر جملة فيها هي الـ **main argument**
In my view / I believe / It is clear that / This article argues that
First / Firstly / The main reason is
Furthermore / Moreover / In addition / Another reason
رأي الناس اللي مخالفين + رد الكاتب عليهم (rebuttal)
Some people argue / Critics claim … However / Nevertheless
الكاتب بيعيد الـ main argument **بكلام تاني** وأحيانًا بيقدّم حل أو نصيحة
In conclusion / To sum up / Therefore / Ultimately

blocks.title: خلي بالك: الـ counter-argument مش رأي الكاتب
blocks.text: لما تلاقي «**Some people argue that** banning phones is the answer» متفتكرش إن ده رأي الكاتب. الكاتب بيعرض رأي الناس التانيين علشان **يرد عليه** بعد كلمة **However**. رأي الكاتب الحقيقي غالبًا **بعد However**.
أنواع الـ Supporting Points والأدلة

text: Writers support their argument with different kinds of evidence: statistics, research findings, expert opinions, examples, personal experience and logical reasons.

rows: **more than 80%** of teenagers fail to meet daily activity levels
**A study found that** teenagers who slept fewer than seven hours felt more anxious.
For example / such as / for instance
**For example**, countdown clocks make shoppers buy quickly.
**When I deleted** the app for a week, I slept better.
**Because** apps earn money from our time, they are designed to keep us scrolling.

blocks.text: الكتاب في Unit 1 بيطلب منك تسأل نفسك: **How convincing do you find this evidence?** يعني الدليل ده مقنع ولا لأ؟ القاعدة البسيطة: الأرقام والدراسات وكلام الخبراء **أقوى** من التجربة الشخصية لوحدها، لأن التجربة الشخصية بتاعة شخص واحد بس.
إزاي تطلّع الـ Main Argument؟ (5 خطوات)

items: **اقرا العنوان** (headline): في مقال الرأي العنوان غالبًا بيلمّح لرأي الكاتب. مثال: «Ban the Ban» يعني الكاتب ضد المنع.
**اقرا أول فقرة وآخر فقرة كويس**: الرأي الأساسي بيتقال في الأول ويتعاد في الآخر.
**دوّر على كلمات الرأي**: I believe / In my view / should / must / it is time to / the real problem is.
**اقرا أول جملة في كل فقرة** (topic sentence): كل واحدة فيهم غالبًا supporting point.
**لخّص في جملة واحدة**: «الكاتب شايف إن … علشان …». لو الجملة دي بتغطي المقال كله يبقى إنت جبت الـ main argument.

blocks.title: إزاي تختار الإجابة الصح في سؤال الـ main idea (MCQ)
items: **Too narrow** (ضيقة أوي): إجابة بتتكلم عن تفصيلة واحدة من فقرة واحدة. ✗
**Too broad** (واسعة أوي): إجابة عامة جدًا ممكن تكون عن أي مقال. ✗
**Extreme** (متطرفة): فيها كلمات زي always / never / all / only / completely والنص مقالش كده. ✗
**Opposite / not mentioned**: عكس رأي الكاتب، أو حاجة مش في النص. ✗
الإجابة الصح = **بتغطي النص كله** + **فيها رأي الكاتب** + **من غير مبالغة**. ✓

blocks.text: نص للشرح (Opinion Article)
النص ده مكتوب للتدريب على موضوع Unit 1 (السوشيال ميديا وصورتنا عن نفسنا). اقراه الأول، وبعدين هنفكّكه سوا.

text: **Filters Are Not the Enemy — Comparison Is**

(1) Every few months, a new headline blames photo filters for teenagers' low self-esteem, and some worried parents respond by deleting their children's apps. In my view, this misses the point. The real damage to young people's self-image comes from the habit of constant comparison, and the answer is not a ban but stronger digital awareness.

(2) First, comparison, not technology, is what makes teenagers feel inadequate. A survey of 1,200 secondary students found that those who often compared their bodies with influencers' photos were twice as likely to report feeling unhappy with their appearance. Interestingly, students who used the same apps mainly to chat with friends did not show the same pattern. This suggests that the problem lies in how teenagers use social media rather than in the apps themselves.

(3) Furthermore, bans rarely change behaviour for long. When one school in the survey blocked social media on its network, more than half of its students simply switched to mobile data. By contrast, a school that ran a six-week media literacy course, in which students analysed edited advertisements and discussed how images are staged, saw a clear drop in negative comparison. Skills stay with students when rules disappear.

(4) Some people argue that platforms, not schools, should solve the problem, since they profit from our attention. It is true that companies must design their apps more responsibly. However, waiting for them to change could take years. Teenagers need protection now, and the quickest protection is knowledge.

(5) Ultimately, deleting an app may feel like a solution, but it only hides the problem. If we teach young people to question what they see online, they will carry that confidence into every screen they ever use.

blocks.text: تفكيك النص خطوة بخطوة

rows: النص بيتكلم عن السوشيال ميديا وصورة المراهقين عن نفسهم.
The real damage … comes from the habit of constant comparison, and the answer is not a ban but stronger digital awareness. (P1)
آخر جملة في الفقرة الأولى، وبعد «In my view». الكاتب شايف إن المشكلة في **المقارنة** مش في الفلاتر، والحل **التوعية** مش المنع.
comparison, not technology, is what makes teenagers feel inadequate (P2)
survey of 1,200 students … twice as likely … (P2)
This suggests that the problem lies in how teenagers use social media (P2)
bans rarely change behaviour for long (P3)
more than half switched to mobile data / media literacy course (P3)
Some people argue that platforms … should solve the problem (P4)
However, waiting for them to change could take years. (P4)
الكاتب بيرد: الشركات ممكن تتأخر سنين.
If we teach young people to question what they see online … (P5)
إعادة الرأي بكلام تاني + نتيجة متوقعة.

items.en: In my view, this misses the point.
items.ar: «this» هنا راجعة على لوم الفلاتر ومسح الأبلكيشنز. الكاتب بيقول: الناس دي فاهمة غلط. ده تمهيد للرأي.

items.en: This suggests that the problem lies in how teenagers use social media rather than in the apps themselves.
items.ar: جملة **شرح (explanation)**: بتقولك الدليل ده معناه إيه. كلمة **suggests** بتدلك إنها استنتاج.

items.en: Skills stay with students when rules disappear.
items.ar: جملة قصيرة في آخر الفقرة بتلخّص الـ supporting point التاني: المهارة بتفضل، القوانين بتروح.

items.en: It is true that companies must design their apps more responsibly.
items.ar: الكاتب **بيعترف** بجزء من رأي المخالفين (concession) قبل ما يرد. ده بيخليه يبان عادل.

items.en: However, waiting for them to change could take years.
items.ar: **الرد (rebuttal)**. بعد However بييجي رأي الكاتب الحقيقي.

items.en: Ultimately, deleting an app may feel like a solution, but it only hides the problem.
items.ar: Ultimately = في الآخر. بداية الخاتمة، وبيعيد الرأي إن المنع مش حل.

blocks.title: أشهر الأخطاء (غلط ← صح)
items: ✗ بتكتب الـ **topic** بدل الـ argument: «The main argument is social media.» ← ✓ «The writer argues that teenagers need digital awareness, not bans, because comparison is the real problem.»
✗ بتختار **تفصيلة** على إنها الفكرة الأساسية: «Half the students switched to mobile data.» ← ✓ دي **evidence** لنقطة واحدة بس.
✗ بتاخد الـ **counter-argument** على إنه رأي الكاتب: «The writer thinks platforms should solve the problem.» ← ✓ ده رأي «some people»، والكاتب رد عليه بـ However.
✗ بتنقل جملة طويلة من النص من غير ما تفهمها لما السؤال يقول «in your own words». ← ✓ لخّص بكلامك: «The writer believes … because …».
✗ بتختار إجابة فيها **always / only / never** والنص مقالش كده. ← ✓ الكاتب قال «rarely» يعني «نادرًا» مش «أبدًا».

blocks.text: إزاي بييجي في الأسئلة؟
الأسئلة في الكتاب والمراجعات بتيجي بالأشكال دي. هنحلّها على النص اللي فوق:
**النوع 1 — Choose the correct answer (main idea):**

text: The main argument of the article is that ______
a. photo filters should be banned on all social media apps
b. teenagers should stop comparing themselves by deleting social media
c. digital awareness, not bans, is the best way to deal with the harm caused by comparison
d. social media companies are the only ones responsible for teenagers' self-image

blocks.text: الإجابة **c**. (a) عكس رأي الكاتب. (b) الكاتب ضد مسح الأبلكيشنز. (d) فيها **only** وده رأي الـ some people اللي الكاتب رد عليه. (c) بتغطي النص كله: المشكلة (المقارنة) + الحل (التوعية).
**النوع 2 — Analyse: What evidence does the writer give to support…?**

text: Q: What evidence does the writer give to show that bans do not work? How convincing is it?

Model answer: The writer explains that when one school blocked social media on its network, more than half of its students simply switched to mobile data. This is quite convincing because it is a real example from a survey, and it shows that students can easily get around rules. However, it is only one school, so more examples would make it stronger.

blocks.text: لاحظ إن الإجابة فيها 3 حاجات: **الدليل من النص** + **رأيك هل هو مقنع** + **السبب**. وده نفس الـ JRE.
**النوع 3 — JRE question:**

text: Q: To what extent do you agree that teaching skills is better than banning apps? Justify your answer with evidence from the text.

Model answer: I largely agree with the writer that teaching skills is more effective than banning apps. This is because a ban only works while the rule exists, but a skill stays with a person for life. According to the text, a school that ran a six-week media literacy course saw a clear drop in negative comparison, while a school that blocked social media saw students switch to mobile data. This shows that knowledge changes behaviour more than rules do.

blocks.text: الإجابة دي: **J** = I largely agree … ، **R** = This is because … ، **E** = According to the text … ، وبعدها شرح يربط (This shows that …).
تدريب
**التدريب الأول:** حدد نوع كل جملة: **Main argument (MA)** ولا **Supporting point (SP)** ولا **Evidence (E)** ولا **Counter-argument (CA)** ولا **Topic (T)**. كل الجمل عن موضوع Unit 1 (النوم والصحة).

items.q: 1. Teenagers' sleep habits
items.a: **T (Topic)** — كلمتين من غير رأي ومن غير فعل.

items.q: 2. Schools should start the day later because teenagers cannot function well early in the morning.
items.a: **MA** — رأي كامل (should) ومعاه سبب عام. ممكن حد يقول «مش موافق».

items.q: 3. Research published in a sleep journal found that students who slept fewer than seven hours reported more anxiety.
items.a: **E** — دراسة ونتيجة (Research … found).

items.q: 4. Some parents argue that a later start would simply make teenagers go to bed later.
items.a: **CA** — «Some parents argue» = رأي الطرف التاني.

items.q: 5. Another reason is that tired students find it difficult to concentrate during lessons.
items.a: **SP** — «Another reason» = سبب بيسند الرأي.

items.q: 6. For example, in one school, test results improved after the first lesson was moved to 9 a.m.
items.a: **E** — مثال (For example).

blocks.text: **التدريب التاني:** اقرا النص ده (Unit 4: التطبيقات والتركيز) وجاوب.

text: **Designed to Keep You Scrolling**

(1) Many people blame themselves when they spend three hours on their phones instead of studying. They think they simply lack willpower. I believe this view is unfair. Most popular apps are carefully designed to capture our attention, so taking control means changing the design around us, not just trying harder.

(2) To begin with, apps make money from our time. The longer we stay, the more advertisements we see. For this reason, designers use features such as infinite scroll, which removes any natural stopping point. A page that never ends gives our brains no signal to put the phone down.

(3) In addition, notifications are timed to pull us back. A former designer at a large technology company once admitted that red notification icons were chosen because red creates a feeling of urgency. Even when the message is unimportant, we feel we must check it.

(4) Critics say that blaming apps is just an excuse and that responsible people should control themselves. Personal responsibility certainly matters. Nevertheless, when the battle is between one tired teenager and a team of experts paid to win his attention, it is hardly a fair fight.

(5) The solution, therefore, is practical. Turning off non-essential notifications, setting daily time limits and keeping the phone out of the bedroom can change the environment so that the better choice becomes the easier choice.

items.q:
7. The main argument of the text is that ______
a. people who spend hours on their phones lack willpower
b. apps are designed to capture attention, so users should change their digital environment
c. technology companies should be banned from using notifications
d. teenagers should never use their phones before studying
items.a: **b** — دي جملة الرأي في آخر الفقرة الأولى (I believe …) ومعاها الحل اللي اتعاد في الخاتمة. (a) ده الرأي اللي الكاتب **رافضه**. (c) و(d) مبالغة ومش في النص.

items.q:
8. Paragraph 3 mainly supports the writer's argument by ______
a. describing how infinite scroll works
b. giving an expert's example of how notifications are designed to pull users back
c. arguing that red is the most attractive colour
d. suggesting that people should turn off their phones
items.a: **b** — الفقرة 3 فيها supporting point (notifications) ودليل من **خبير سابق** (a former designer). (a) ده الفقرة 2.

items.q:
9. Choose an appropriate heading for paragraph 4.
a. Why Willpower Does Not Matter
b. An Unfair Fight
c. The History of Smartphones
d. How Advertisements Make Money
items.a: **b** — الفقرة فيها رأي المخالفين والرد عليه بإن المعركة «hardly a fair fight». (a) غلط لأن الكاتب قال «Personal responsibility certainly matters».

items.q: 10. Find a sentence in paragraph 1 that states the writer's main argument.
items.a: «**Most popular apps are carefully designed to capture our attention, so taking control means changing the design around us, not just trying harder.**» — جت بعد I believe this view is unfair، وفيها الرأي والحل. (لو كتبت الجملتين مع بعض «I believe this view is unfair. Most popular apps…» تبقى إجابة صح برضه.)

items.q: 11. What counter-argument does the writer mention, and how does he respond to it?
items.a: The writer mentions that critics think blaming apps is an excuse and people should control themselves. He responds that personal responsibility matters, **but** one tired teenager cannot easily win against a team of experts paid to win his attention. — لاحظ إن الكاتب **اعترف** بجزء وبعدين **رد** بـ Nevertheless.

items.q:
12. State whether the statement is True (T) or False (F). Justify your answer.
The writer believes that personal responsibility is not important at all.
items.a: **False** — Justification: «**Personal responsibility certainly matters.**» الكاتب قال إنها مهمة، بس مش كفاية لوحدها.

items.q:
13. State whether the statement is True (T) or False (F). Justify your answer.
According to the writer, infinite scroll removes a natural point at which users might stop.
items.a: **True** — Justification: «infinite scroll, which **removes any natural stopping point**.»

items.q:
14. Which type of evidence does the writer use in paragraph 3?
a. a statistic  b. a personal experience  c. an expert's statement  d. a survey
items.a: **c** — «A former designer … once admitted» = كلام شخص من جوه المجال، يعني expert.

blocks.text: **التدريب التالت:** في كل سؤال اختار أنهي جملة تنفع **main argument** لمقال، وليه الباقي لأ.

items.q:
15. Topic: food waste (Unit 4)
a. Food waste.
b. Egyptian families throw away a large amount of food during Ramadan.
c. Families can reduce food waste by planning meals and buying only what they need.
d. Bread is the food most often thrown away.
items.a: **c** — فيها رأي وحل (can reduce … by …). (a) topic بس. (b) و(d) معلومات (evidence) ملهاش رأي.

items.q:
16. Topic: climate change (Unit 5)
a. Temperatures have risen in the last century.
b. Young people have the power to push governments towards cleaner energy.
c. Climate change and the planet.
d. The Maldives is a group of islands.
items.a: **b** — رأي ممكن تتناقش فيه. (a) و(d) حقائق. (c) topic.

items.q:
17. Topic: sales and discounts (Unit 4)
a. Sales always trick every shopper.
b. Many shops use countdown clocks.
c. Sale events often encourage people to spend more, not less, so shoppers should make a list before they go.
d. Shopping.
items.a: **c** — رأي متوازن + نصيحة. (a) فيها **always / every** مبالغة. (b) evidence. (d) topic.

items.q:
18. Topic: mindfulness (Unit 1)
a. Mindfulness means paying attention to the present moment.
b. Mindfulness should be part of the school timetable because it reduces stress.
c. Yoga is one form of mindfulness.
d. Ten minutes a day.
items.a: **b** — رأي (should) + سبب. (a) **تعريف**. (c) مثال. (d) تفصيلة.

blocks.text: **التدريب الرابع (JRE والكتابة):** جاوب في 4-5 جمل.

items.q: 19. In the text «Designed to Keep You Scrolling», how convincing is the writer's evidence? Justify your answer.
items.a: Model: The evidence is partly convincing. The example of the former designer is strong because he worked inside the industry and knows how apps are designed. However, the writer gives no statistics about how much time people actually lose. Therefore, a study or survey would make the argument more convincing. — لاحظ: رأي + نقطة قوة + نقطة ضعف + اقتراح.

items.q: 20. Write the main argument of «Filters Are Not the Enemy — Comparison Is» in your own words in ONE sentence.
items.a: Model: The writer believes that teenagers feel bad about their appearance mainly because they compare themselves with others online, so schools should teach them media skills instead of banning apps. — جملة واحدة فيها **المشكلة** و**الحل** من غير نسخ.

items.q: 21. Add ONE more supporting point (with evidence or an example) that the writer of «Designed to Keep You Scrolling» could use.
items.a: Model: Another supporting point is that apps reward us with likes, which work like small prizes. For example, many teenagers check their posts again and again to see how many likes they have received. — أي سبب منطقي مربوط بالتصميم + مثال.

items.q: 22. To what extent are users responsible for the time they spend on apps? Use evidence from the text.
items.a: Model: Users are partly responsible, but not fully. The writer admits that «personal responsibility certainly matters». However, he explains that apps use infinite scroll and red notifications to pull us back. This shows that users need to change their settings, because willpower alone is not enough. — J + R + E + شرح.

blocks.title: ملخص الدرس في سطرين
items: **Topic** = الموضوع (كلمتين). **Main argument** = رأي الكاتب في جملة كاملة (أنا موافق / مش موافق).
الرأي بيتقال غالبًا **آخر الفقرة الأولى** ويتعاد في **الخاتمة**. وكلماته: I believe / In my view / should / the real problem is.
كل فقرة في النص = **supporting point** + **evidence** (رقم، دراسة، خبير، مثال) + **شرح**.
«Some people argue…» = **counter-argument** مش رأي الكاتب. رأيه بعد **However / Nevertheless**.
في الـ MCQ ارفض الإجابة **الضيقة** و**الواسعة** و**المبالغ فيها** (always / only / never) واختار اللي بتغطي النص كله.
